chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: The drowned one is washed.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْغَرِيقُ: The drowned one (deceased who died in water)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual ruling for washing a person who dies by drowning?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the drowned individual is treated as a standard deceased Muslim, requiring only the ordinary ritual bath (ghusl) without the complexities of additional purification rites often debated in fiqh. It reflects the Imami juristic view that death by drowning does not invalidate the ritual purity status, distinguishing it from cases where the body is fragmented or lost. This ruling underscores the consistency of burial rites in Shia tradition, emphasizing simplicity and adherence to the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams.
